# Frame and leaf spring bracket rust

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove rear rubber molding and scrape loose paint while checking for uneven surfaces. [t275]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the rubber door molding from both rear doors.
2. Scrape away loose paint and rust residue, noting that wire brushes may wear out quickly on the inside lip.

_Procedure reported by [t275]._

## Tools

- Wire brush [t275]
- Dremel [t275]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Run fingers gently along the edge where the molding sits to feel for bumps or uneven surfaces. [t275]
- Check both sides, as rust may start on one side but affect the other. [t275]

## Common mistakes

- Wearing out wire brushes too fast due to the sharp inside lip of the door opening. [t275]
